Sean / team —

I reviewed MercuryPay's questions and sketched a one-page plain-language DPA summary (attached as a redline in MercuryPay_DPA_Questions_v3.docx). High-level notes:

- Keep public language focused on (1) what data we process, (2) where it may be processed, (3) subprocessors and how we manage them, and (4) customer controls (residency toggle, retention settings). Avoid legalese like "may" and "shall" without context; use "we may transfer" only when necessary and follow with mitigation e.g., standard contractual clauses.
- Subprocessors: list should be summarized by function (e.g., "cloud infra — US/EU, logging — US only"). Procurement teams appreciate geography-first summaries ("data stays in region unless you opt into cross-border features").
- DPA one-pager structure: 1) Short summary (2–3 lines), 2) What we process + retention, 3) Subprocessors (function + region), 4) Transfers & safeguards (SCCs, encryption in transit/rest), 5) How to request data residency or audit logs, 6) Contact & next steps.

Suggested 250-char console blurb (variant A - customer-facing):

"We store and process API inputs to provide inference. Customers can select regional hosting (US, EU, APAC). We use SCCs and encryption for cross-border transfers; a full DPA and subprocessor list are available on request."

Shorter variant (variant B - procurement portal):

"Regional hosting options (US, EU, APAC). Cross-border transfers protected by SCCs; full DPA and subprocessor list available."

I've attached the annotated doc and a quick data-flow PNG (redwood-data-flow.png) that maps where model inference runs vs. telemetry/logging subprocessors. Laura: I've left a procurement-friendly note suggesting we proactively offer the residency toggle as a configurable term for enterprise contracts.

Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security — Redwood Inference

Attachments: MercuryPay_DPA_Questions_v3.docx (annotated), redwood-data-flow.png (png)

Thanks Kim — good direction. A couple product notes to keep messaging accurate:

- "Regional hosting" needs a tiny clarification for the UI: Hosted API customers can pick a default region for model execution; certain features (e.g., telemetry/usage analytics) may be processed in our control plane (US by default) unless the customer opts into Dedicated/Private.
- For the short portal blurb, propose two tight options (<=250 chars):
  * Option 1 (customer-friendly): "Choose regional inference (US, EU, APAC). Control-plane logs are stored in the region you select for Dedicated/Private; hosted accounts may have control-plane metadata in the US. Transfers are protected by SCCs."
  * Option 2 (procurement-friendly): "Regional inference by region. Cross-border transfers use SCCs; subprocessor functions and locations available on request."

- UX constraint: procurement portals sometimes truncate at ~300 chars; we'll deliver both a 250c and 320c version so Mercury can copy whichever fits.

I'll attach the console-blurbs doc with the two length variants (redwood-console-blurbs-v1.md).

-Karthik
Product Manager, Platform — Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood-console-blurbs-v1.md (md)

Hi Lisa / Tom —

Appreciate the quick turnaround on the procurement questions. Attached are three items for your review: 1) a one-page plain-language DPA summary (extracted from the annotated doc), 2) two console blurb variants (250-char and ~320-char), and 3) a one-slide data flow that maps subprocessors by function and region.

Key points in the one-pager:
- What we process: API inputs and derived outputs for inference; customer-managed keys are supported for Private deployments.
- Where it can be processed: regional inference (US, EU, APAC) for model execution. Control-plane metadata and certain analytics may be processed in the US unless you opt into Dedicated/Private hosting.
- Subprocessors summarized by function and region (cloud infra — US/EU, logging & analytics — US; model hosting partners listed in full in our subprocessor map on request).
- Cross-border transfers: we use EU Standard Contractual Clauses (SCCs) and encryption in transit/rest; we can include additional contractual safeguards on a per-deal basis.

Console blurb (250-char variant):
"Choose regional inference (US, EU, APAC). Cross-border transfers protected by SCCs; full DPA and subprocessor list available on request. Contact privacy@redwood.ai for residency or audit requests."

320-char variant (for procurement portal paste):
"Regional inference options (US, EU, APAC). Control-plane metadata may be processed in the US for hosted plans; Dedicated/Private keep processing in your region. Cross-border transfers are covered by SCCs and encryption. Full DPA & subprocessor map available on request."

Next steps: please confirm which blurb length you prefer and whether procurement needs the full subprocessor CSV or the summarized function+region map. Happy to hop on a 20-min call Monday if that helps move it through review quickly.

Best —
Sean Gallagher
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference

Attachments: Redwood_DPA_OnePager_MercuryPay.pdf (pdf), redwood-console-blurbs-v1.md (md), redwood-data-flow.png (png)
